headline: Apple adds Mac AI-agent controls as Signal moves to block AI screenshots
summary: Apple detailed new macOS permission and disk-access controls limiting what AI agents can do on Macs. Separately, Signal began blocking screenshots by default in its apps to stop AI agents from capturing conversations, extending a restriction it first added because of Microsoft Recall. One outlet said Apple, Google and Microsoft were all criticized for inadequate developer controls against AI agents.

claims.statement: Apple detailed new permission, warning and transparency controls coming to macOS to address AI-agent risks.

sources.quote: Following an October announcement, Apple has detailed new permission controls, warnings, and transparency features coming to macOS 27.3 to address risks posed by AI agents and other apps.

claims.statement: Apple's new controls will limit AI agents' access to Mac disk storage.

sources.quote: Apple adds new disk controls to prevent AI agents from running amok

claims.statement: Signal is restricting or blocking screenshots in its apps to limit AI agents' ability to capture content.

sources.quote: Signal to restrict screenshots over AI agent concerns – again
Signal now blocks screenshots by default to stymie AI agents
Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in both its Android and iOS apps.

claims.statement: Signal previously limited screenshots because of Microsoft Recall.

sources.quote: The messaging app similarly limited screenshots because of Microsoft Recall last year.

claims.statement: Critics said Signal's fix is incomplete and called for an opt-out mechanism for developers.

sources.quote: It describes the fix as incomplete and calls for a simple way for developers to opt out of AI snooping.

claims.statement: Apple, Google and Microsoft were criticized for failing to give developers adequate AI-agent controls.

sources.quote: Apple, Google, and Microsoft called out for failing to provide developers with adequate AI agent controls
